newsitem.title: USA: WTO challenge possible on apples to Japan - USTR.
newsitem.headline: WTO challenge possible on apples to Japan - USTR.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Monday the United States might file a world trade complaint if negotiations fail to solve a dispute with Japan over apple exports.
The nations were to hold a negotiating session later this week. Barshefsky told reporters that Japan imposed unduly long testing periods, lasting about two years, before allowing apple imports.
"We'll see how those go," she said, referring to the bilateral talks. "But if they don't go well, we will consider seriously utilizing" the World Trade Organization dispute process.
Three varieties of U.S. apples are allowed into the Japanese market at present and exporters want to sell three additional varieties, she said.
